smell_validity.evidence: Only 3 of 13 ConnOps members (sbuf_event, handle_complete_packet, disconnect) are dispatched from sbuf.c/proto.c; the rest exist to catalogue kinds, forcing 3/2/7 NULL slots in the client/server/peer tables plus wrapper adapters like server_finish_login. Peer sockets even reach a NULL handle_complete_packet via SBUF_EV_PKT_CALLBACK. Beside the untouched, uniformly-wired SBufIO table, the fault and its cost are unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every new connection kind must catalogue 13 capabilities, and single-kind logic (login/work protocol, pool selection, cancellation) is published through a shared contract, blurring ownership between the client.c/server.c state machines and shared dispatch; NULL slots are silent obligations rather than safety. Slimming restores a clear long-term boundary where shared code owns only the genuinely dispatched operations.

development_plausibility.evidence: Highly idiomatic: ConnOps mirrors the existing struct SBufIO idiom in the same struct, registration reuses the prior sbuf_init call sites, adapters preserve Asserts and move infobuf to a local, and peer_id selection sits exactly where db->peer_id becomes known. Only undispatched client-shaped members (startup_pool, cancel_request) read as planted breadth rather than organic growth.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Names the smell, enumerates the exact scaffolding to remove (trivial wrappers, table-only declarations, empty slots, special-case registration), protects genuinely dispatched helpers, and forbids both realistic wrong repairs — regressing to is_server_socket branching and merging genuinely distinct kinds — while freezing wire packets, logs, state transitions, auth modes, peer cancellation and test outcomes, keeping implementation shape open.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes need separate decisions: which members survive (from real sbuf.c/proto.c dispatch sites), adapter disposition (disconnect wrappers stay, finish_login wrappers go), restoring event-arm bodies in client.c/server.c, and the peer kind's fate without a NULL slot. Adapter re-inlining alone is one repeated rule, so 'each purpose needs a different decision' (5) is not met.

localization_burden.evidence: Classifying the peer site requires combining sbuf's packet-callback trigger with the peer_id-selected registration in launch_new_connection, not inspection at the site alone. Decoys need exclusion: the SBufIO ops field assigned beside conn_ops in sbuf_init, and genuinely dispatched helpers (client_handle_complete_packet, both disconnect adapters) that resemble table filler.

repair_coordination.evidence: Interlocking rules: keeping only shared-dispatched operations forces a new way for objects.c's peer registration to express 'no complete-packet handling' without a NULL slot, while the sbuf_init mechanism choice couples header, both constructors and the peer overwrite site. Repairing the interface alone silently redefines peer dispatch behavior.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform rule — delete each member with no shared dispatch site together with its initializers and slot-filling wrappers — cleans connops.h, the client and server tables and most adapters, roughly 60-75% of locations, without per-site behavioral decisions. It fixes neither peer_server_ops' complete-packet slot nor the peer_id registration special-case.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A concrete wrong edit — removing the peer special-case so peer sockets use server_conn_ops — compiles and passes ordinary traffic, cancellations and tests; it diverges only when a peer connection receives a packet exceeding the sbuf callback threshold. Re-inlining server_tls_ready could silently drop its Assert. No test records establish the unchecked multi-path failures needed for 4.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
